assessment.nobel_worthiness: Surfactant-templated ordered mesoporous silica (M41S/MCM-41, plus FSM-16 and SBA/CMK-type extensions) opened a new pore-size regime beyond zeolites and enabled a large family of ordered mesoporous solids, supports and catalysts. It is original, clearly defined, and structurally well characterized, with broad use in catalysis, adsorption and nanocasting. This sits close to my own field of porous framework materials.
assessment.attribution: Mobil's Kresge and Beck made the decisive M41S discovery; Ryoo extended ordered mesoporosity to larger-pore and carbon replicas and to mechanistic understanding. Inagaki's earlier FSM-16 and Stucky/Zhao's large-pore SBA work are real competing claims, so a three-person prize leaves out serious contributors.
assessment.maturity: Thirty-plus years of independent confirmation and widespread industrial and academic use; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Priority between Mobil's M41S and Inagaki's FSM-16 may be contested.
Whether Ryoo or Stucky/Zhao is the better third laureate is unresolved.
I am relying on memory of the history and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Induced-proximity protein degradation, through PROTACs and molecular glue degraders such as thalidomide analogues acting via cereblon, created a new therapeutic modality and a new way to control protein levels chemically. The concept is original and is now translating into clinical candidates, giving chemical and societal impact.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and developed PROTACs. Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target, which underlies the glue-degrader mechanism. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and others are also major contributors, so the credit allocation is crowded and the field is two partly distinct discoveries.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is well supported by structures and cell biology, and many groups confirm it. Clinical validation is still emerging, so some may argue it is slightly early.
uncertainties: PROTACs and molecular glues may merit different recognition.
Clinical approval is not yet established.
Selecting three laureates from a crowded credit list is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers took solar cell efficiency from a few percent to over 25 percent within about a decade, a very rapid change in materials chemistry. Its structure-property relationships and defect tolerance are of broad scientific interest.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported perovskite-sensitized cells; Park's solid-state cell and Snaith's thin-film and mesosuperstructured work were decisive for efficiency. Kanatzidis, Seok and Grätzel also have strong claims, and the proposed trio omits some.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency results are independently confirmed worldwide. Long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial viability remain unresolved, so some committee members may see the work as premature.
uncertainties: Operational stability and commercialization are unproven.
Credit is contested among at least six people.
Early reports had hysteresis and reproducibility problems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: MXenes form a new large family of 2D transition-metal carbides and nitrides derived by selective etching of MAX phases. They show tunable composition, metallic conductivity and hydrophilic surfaces, with applications in energy storage, EMI shielding and catalysis. As a structural and inorganic materials chemist I value a new materials class with designed architecture and wide function.
assessment.attribution: Naguib, Gogotsi and Barsoum authored the 2011 and 2012 foundational work, and the credited trio is clean and compact. Gogotsi's later development of the field is large.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by hundreds of groups and the structures are well established by diffraction and electron microscopy. Real-world applications are still developing, so recognition may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Technological impact has not yet matured.
The balance between discovery credit and later field-building is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Metal-directed self-assembly gives discrete coordination cages and capsules with defined cavities, enabling host-guest chemistry, confined catalysis and molecular recognition. Fujita's crystalline sponge method also supports structure determination. The structural logic is rigorous and the architecture-to-function link is strong.
assessment.attribution: Fujita, Raymond and Stang each independently established design principles for discrete coordination assemblies. Nitschke and Ward are important later contributors, so the line is generous but plausible.
assessment.maturity: Decades of confirmation by structural data. Applications are less developed than the concept, but the field is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 1987 supramolecular prize may reduce novelty in some eyes.
Practical impact is mostly in fundamental science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and molecular-sieve catalysts, including structure-directing agents, new frameworks and engineered active sites, underpins refining, petrochemistry and emission control. It has major industrial impact and exemplifies structure-function design.
assessment.attribution: Davis, Corma and Zones made central contributions in organic structure-directing agents, new framework discovery and catalysis. Jihong Yu and Tsapatsis are also strong, so credit is spread over a diffuse field.
assessment.maturity: A mature, widely confirmed field. The challenge is that the discovery is incremental and cumulative, with no single decisive breakthrough.
uncertainties: Strong competing credit claims from other zeolite chemists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structure and mechanism of nitrogenase address one of the most important biological transformations and its unusual FeMo cofactor with interstitial carbide. Crystallography, spectroscopy and trapped intermediates have defined the active-site chemistry. Its structural evidence is the strength, but turnover mechanism is still debated.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the crystallographic structure of the MoFe protein and FeMo cofactor; Einsle located the central carbide; Seefeldt and Dean carried out the mechanistic and biochemical work. Ribbe's contribution is also notable, so the allocation is not straightforward.
assessment.maturity: The structure is well established and independently reproduced. The catalytic mechanism remains incompletely resolved, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Credit among five groups is hard to divide.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at XFELs gave structures from micro- and nanocrystals at room temperature and time-resolved dynamics, circumventing radiation damage. As an enabling methodology for crystals too small for conventional sources, it is close to my interests in structure determination from tiny crystals.
assessment.attribution: Chapman, Fromme and Schlichting were central to the proof of principle and development, with Hajdu proposing the diffraction-before-destruction concept. Hajdu's omission from a three-person set is uncomfortable.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced at several XFELs and in a growing set of time-resolved studies. Impact is still concentrated at large facilities and applications are still developing.
uncertainties: Hajdu versus another laureate in a three-person prize is a hard choice.
